advances: Extends nonprimitive chord reassignment from log-affine profiles to every finite globally extendable log-concave table. The reassignment pays into a reflected-minimum kernel discounted by one half of the midpoint curvature, so its mass controls the accepted curvature-cutoff score without any dimension-dependent loss. Separating primitive and nonprimitive images improves the combined congestion coefficient to \(\max\{4,2+e^L\}\). The resulting exact reduction preserves the entire parity-collision product mass and gives a pointwise actual-body depth consumer. The remaining primitive retained-product condition is stated as a conditional resource bound, not as a uniform theorem.
author: research-agent
external_sources: None. The actual global extension, upper semicontinuity, curvature-depth consumer, and ternary obstruction are used through the declared accepted facts. The discounted contraction, its congestion bounds, the diagonal accounting, and the exact parity-resource reduction are proved above.
proof:
Global log-concavity implies that every integer point on the segment between two positive sites is positive. Applying it at a midpoint gives \(w_j^2\ge w_{j+v}w_{j-v}\) for every feasible reflected pair. Thus all the stated logarithms and curvatures are finite on their domains, \(\Delta_j\ge0\), and \(\mathcal U_j\) is finite, even, and contains zero. Also \(\alpha_j(0)=w_j\) and \(\Delta_j(0)=\tau_j(0)=0\). For each \(j\), replacing a cutoff \(s\) by the largest member of \(\{\Delta_j(v):v\in\mathcal U_j\}\) not exceeding it preserves the numerator and decreases the denominator. This finite set contains zero, so every maximum defining \(K_j\) is attained, and finiteness of \(A\) gives attainment of \(K\). This is also the same attainment argument used in `997f7c3a0c4804e4`.

The map \((j,v)\mapsto(j+v,j-v)\) is a bijection from feasible oriented reflected pairs to ordered positive endpoint pairs of the same parity. Its inverse is \((x,y)\mapsto((x+y)/2,(x-y)/2)\). The inverse center is an integer by parity and is positive by global log-concavity. A diagonal endpoint pair occurs once, at zero displacement. It follows that \(P_{\mathrm{tot}}=\sum_bW_b^2=qW^2\). Cauchy-Schwarz gives \(W^2\le2^n\sum_bW_b^2\); expansion of \((\sum_bW_b)^2\) also gives \(q\le1\). This verifies the parity identity with the exact normalization of `997f7c3a0c4804e4`, without any log-affine replacement of endpoint products by midpoint squares.

For each positive center the finite layer-cake calculation is

\[
\begin{aligned}
E_j
&=\sum_{v\in\mathcal U_j}\alpha_j(v)
\int_{\Delta_j(v)}^\infty\tfrac12e^{-s/2}\,ds\\
&=\int_0^\infty\tfrac12e^{-s/2}B_j^\Delta(s)\,ds\\
&\le K_j(w)\int_0^\infty\tfrac12e^{-s/2}(1+s)\,ds
=3K_j(w).
\end{aligned}
\tag{5}
\]

The two moments in the last integral are one and two. The integral beginning at zero equals one, so zero displacement contributes exactly \(w_j\) to \(E_j\); it is not lost at a cutoff boundary. The sum is finite, which justifies the interchange. Multiplying by \(w_j\), summing over \(j\), and using \(K_j(w)\le K(w)\) proves \(\mathscr R\le3K(w)W\).

Let \(\mathcal E\) be the finite set of unordered two-element subsets \(e=\{x,y\}\subset A\) with same-parity endpoints. For \(e\in\mathcal E\), put \(j_e:=(x+y)/2\), \(p_e:=w_xw_y\), and \(r_e:=\sqrt{w_xw_y}\min\{w_x,w_y\}\). These definitions do not depend on the ordering of the endpoints. If \(v=(x-y)/2\), the exact cancellation identity is

\[
w_{j_e}\alpha_{j_e}(v)e^{-\Delta_{j_e}(v)/2}
=\sqrt{w_xw_y}\min\{w_x,w_y\}=r_e.
\tag{6}
\]

Each unordered pair contributes exactly two oriented displacements at its unique midpoint. The diagonal contributes exactly \(D_w\) to both product mass and \(\mathscr R\). Accordingly, \(\mathscr R-D_w=2\sum_{e\in\mathcal E}r_e\) and \(P_{\mathrm{tot}}-D_w=2\sum_{e\in\mathcal E}p_e\). Let \(\mathcal E_{\mathrm{prim}}\) and \(\mathcal E_{\mathrm{np}}\) partition \(\mathcal E\) according as \((x-y)/2\) is primitive or nonprimitive. Then \(P_{\mathrm{np}}=2\sum_{e\in\mathcal E_{\mathrm{np}}}p_e\) and \(P_{\mathrm{prim}}=2\sum_{e\in\mathcal E_{\mathrm{prim}}}p_e\).

Fix lexicographic order on \(\mathbb Z^n\). Orient every source \(e\in\mathcal E_{\mathrm{np}}\) by calling its higher-weight endpoint \(x\); in a weight tie choose its lexicographically larger endpoint as \(x\). Call its other endpoint \(y\). There is a unique representation \(y=x-2ku\), where \(k\ge2\) is the greatest common divisor of the absolute coordinates of \((x-y)/2\) and \(u=(x-y)/(2k)\) is primitive. The direction \(u\) here has the role of the vector called \(d\) in `3bd24ddc8a30dd00`; the symbol \(d\) in this packet remains the continuous dimension of an actual body.

Set \(k':=\lceil k/2\rceil\), \(y':=x-2k'u\), \(j':=x-k'u\), and \(\Phi(e):=\{x,y'\}\). Both \(y'\) and \(j'\) are integer points of \([x,y]\), hence have positive weights. The image endpoints are distinct and have the same parity, so \(\Phi(e)\in\mathcal E\), with midpoint \(j'\). For \(k=2m\), the inequality \(3k'\le2k\) reads \(3m\le4m\). For \(k=2m+1\), where \(m\ge1\), it reads \(3m+3\le4m+2\). Thus \(t:=k'/k\) belongs to \([1/2,2/3]\).

Write \(a:=w_x\), \(b:=w_y\), and \(c:=w_{y'}\). The source orientation gives \(a\ge b>0\), and global log-concavity at \(y'=(1-t)x+ty\) gives \(c\ge a^{1-t}b^t\). If \(c\le a\), then

\[
r_{\Phi(e)}=a^{1/2}c^{3/2}
\ge a^{2-3t/2}b^{3t/2}
=ab(a/b)^{1-3t/2}\ge ab.
\tag{7}
\]

The last inequality uses \(a/b\ge1\) and \(t\le2/3\). If instead \(c\ge a\), then \(r_{\Phi(e)}=a^{3/2}c^{1/2}\ge a^2\ge ab\). In both cases, \(p_e\le r_{\Phi(e)}\). By (6), the right side is exactly \(w_{j'}\alpha_{j'}(k'u)e^{-\Delta_{j'}(k'u)/2}\). No upper bound on the image curvature has been assumed: its exponential discount is already included in the identity.

The weight order of the image endpoints can differ from the source order, so it is not used to reconstruct a source. Given an image \(e'\in\mathcal E\), there are at most two choices of which endpoint was the original \(x\). Once one is chosen, the other is \(y'\), and \(k'\) is uniquely recovered as the greatest common divisor of the absolute coordinates of \((x-y')/2\); then \(u=(x-y')/(2k')\) is also fixed. A possible source must have \(k\in\{2k'-1,2k'\}\), with \(k\ge2\). Each such value determines at most one source, \(\{x,x-2ku\}\). Conditions on support, source weight order, and the tie rule can only remove possibilities.

Consequently, every nonprimitive image has at most four sources. A primitive image has \(k'=1\); then \(k=1\) is excluded, so only \(k=2\) is possible for each choice of original endpoint, giving at most two sources. There are no diagonal images. In particular, summing \(p_e\le r_{\Phi(e)}\) with the uniform bound four and then restoring the two orientations gives

\[
P_{\mathrm{np}}
=2\sum_{e\in\mathcal E_{\mathrm{np}}}p_e
\le2\sum_{e'\in\mathcal E}|\Phi^{-1}(e')|r_{e'}
\le8\sum_{e'\in\mathcal E}r_{e'}
=4(\mathscr R-D_w).
\tag{8}
\]

This proves the remaining assertion in (1), with the diagonal excluded from the reassignment at every step.

Now fix \(L\ge0\). Partition \(\mathcal E_{\mathrm{prim}}\) into \(\mathcal E_{\mathrm{good}}(L)\) and \(\mathcal E_{\mathrm{bad}}(L)\) according as \(\tfrac12|\log(w_x/w_y)|\le L\) or \(>L\). This absolute value is \(|\tau_{j_e}((x-y)/2)|\) for either ordering of the endpoints. Directly from the definitions,
\(p_e/r_e=\sqrt{\max\{w_x,w_y\}/\min\{w_x,w_y\}}=e^{|\tau_{j_e}((x-y)/2)|}\).
Thus \(p_e\le e^Lr_e\) on \(\mathcal E_{\mathrm{good}}(L)\), and \(P_{\mathrm{bad}}(L)=2\sum_{e\in\mathcal E_{\mathrm{bad}}(L)}p_e\).

Use the refined preimage counts, two on primitive images and four on nonprimitive images, before adding this good-primitive charge. They give

\[
\begin{aligned}
P_{\mathrm{tot}}-P_{\mathrm{bad}}(L)
&=D_w+2\sum_{e\in\mathcal E_{\mathrm{np}}}p_e
+2\sum_{e\in\mathcal E_{\mathrm{good}}(L)}p_e\\
&\le D_w+8\sum_{e'\in\mathcal E_{\mathrm{np}}}r_{e'}
+2\sum_{e'\in\mathcal E_{\mathrm{prim}}}
\bigl(2+e^L\mathbf1_{\{e'\in\mathcal E_{\mathrm{good}}(L)\}}\bigr)r_{e'}\\
&\le D_w+2\gamma(L)\sum_{e'\in\mathcal E}r_{e'}\\
&=\gamma(L)\mathscr R-(\gamma(L)-1)D_w.
\end{aligned}
\tag{9}
\]

Indeed, the coefficient per image inside twice the pair sum is at most four for a nonprimitive image, at most \(2+e^L\) for a good primitive image, and at most two for a bad primitive image. This accounts for every possible overlap between a contracted image and a retained original pair. Neither charge reaches the diagonal. Substituting \(\mathscr R\le3K(w)W\) proves (2). Rearranging, retaining \(P_{\mathrm{tot}}=qW^2\), and only then using \(q\ge2^{-n}\), proves (3). The first numerator in (3) is positive: \(P_{\mathrm{tot}}-P_{\mathrm{bad}}(L)\ge D_w>0\). The last, coarser numerator is not assumed positive when no resource condition is available.

If \(P_{\mathrm{tot}}-P_{\mathrm{bad}}(L)\ge\eta\,2^{-n}W^2\), discard only the nonnegative diagonal term in (3) to obtain the stated conditional score bound. If the baseline condition holds with \(\rho<1\), then \(P_{\mathrm{tot}}\ge2^{-n}W^2\) gives the retained-product condition with \(\eta=1-\rho\). None of these steps replaces the exact parity resource before stating the stronger conclusion. All normalizations are also homogeneous: multiplying the table by a positive constant multiplies \(E_j,K_j,K,W\) by that constant, multiplies the product masses and \(\mathscr R\) by its square, and leaves \(\Delta_j,\tau_j\) unchanged.

For the actual-body application, compactness of the projection of \(C\) gives finite positive integer support. Accepted fact `b563a1eb51a20cd2` proves that the real-base function \(g(x):=\operatorname{vol}_d(C_x)\) is a finite-valued globally log-concave extension of the actual table, including its zeros and lower-rank positive integer support. Thus the scalar hypotheses apply without altering the body or any fiber weight.

The root-concavity underlying this applicability has the required direction on every contracted chord. For positive endpoint fibers at real bases \(x,y\), convexity of the same \(C\) gives \((1-t)C_x+tC_y\subseteq C_{(1-t)x+ty}\). The root-volume midpoint inequality recorded in the proof of `280b299bc1e87c14` applies to the segment restriction of this body, as in the proof of `b563a1eb51a20cd2`. That restriction is a compact convex body in \(\mathbb R^{1+d}\) when \(x\ne y\): a positive endpoint fiber provides \(d+1\) affinely independent points and a point at the other endpoint supplies the additional dimension. Iterating the midpoint-root inequality gives its dyadic versions, and the upper semicontinuity of \(g\) proved in `b563a1eb51a20cd2` extends them to every \(0<t<1\). Hence

\[
g((1-t)x+ty)^{1/d}
\ge(1-t)g(x)^{1/d}+tg(y)^{1/d}
\ge g(x)^{(1-t)/d}g(y)^{t/d}.
\tag{10}
\]

The last inequality is weighted arithmetic-geometric mean. Equal bases give equality, and a zero endpoint needs no root-volume argument for the log-concavity inequality, whose right-hand side is then zero. Raising (10) to the power \(d\) gives exactly the interpolation bound used in (7). Thus all source, image, and midpoint weights in the application are actual fibers of one common body; no independently assigned volume table or dimension-dependent replacement is involved.

Choose once and for all a center \(j\) attaining \(K(w)\), and a finite curvature cutoff \(s_\star\) attaining \(K_j(w)\). These choices do not involve the primitive tilt cutoff \(L\) or a halfspace. Apply the fixed-center theorem of `280b299bc1e87c14` with its even thinning \(q_v:=\alpha_j(v)\mathbf1_{\{v\in\mathcal U_j,\ \Delta_j(v)\le s_\star\}}\), setting it to zero off \(\mathcal U_j\). Then \(0\le q_v\le\alpha_j(v)\), its total mass is \(M_q=B_j^\Delta(s_\star)\ge w_j>0\), and its average curvature satisfies \(\overline\Delta_{j,q}\le s_\star\). All fibers, volumes, oriented sums, and the zero displacement have the predecessor's exact normalization. It supplies one \(p^\star=(j,x^\star)\in S\) with

\[
h_S(p^\star)
\ge\frac{\ell B_j^\Delta(s_\star)}{16(\overline\Delta_{j,q}+\log2)}
\ge\frac{\ell B_j^\Delta(s_\star)}{16(1+s_\star)}
=\frac{\ell}{16}K(w).
\tag{11}
\]

The predecessor's conclusion is pointwise and applies to every closed ambient halfspace containing this point, including vertical and boundary cases. Combining (11) with (3) gives (4) for every \(L\) at that same point. The conditional depth and the displayed choice of \(c_0\) follow by substitution; fixed \(L,\eta\) make it an absolute positive constant below \(1/e\). If \(W=0\), every mixed-integer halfspace mass is nonnegative, giving the asserted trivial case.

Finally, the log-affine specialization in the statement follows from \(\log w_{j+v}+\log w_{j-v}=2\log w_j\), and verifies every alias to `3bd24ddc8a30dd00`, including its oriented primitive masses and zero term. Its ternary example has the global extension equal to \(\exp(-\log2\sum_i x_i)\) on \([0,2]^n\) and zero outside that convex box. It therefore belongs to the present class. The accepted divergence of its \(\widetilde T_{\mathrm{bad}}(L)/(2^{-n}\widetilde W^2)\), together with the exact alias \(P_{\mathrm{bad}}(L)=\widetilde T_{\mathrm{bad}}(L)\), proves the asserted failure of the baseline bad-mass condition without repeating that calculation. The accepted result does not bound the retained difference \(P_{\mathrm{tot}}-P_{\mathrm{bad}}(L)\) from above by a vanishing multiple of the baseline, so no such obstruction or uniform retained-product theorem is inferred here.
statement:
Let \(n\ge1\) be an integer, let \(w=(w_z)_{z\in\mathbb Z^n}\) be a nonzero, nonnegative, finitely supported table of finite real numbers, and put \(A:=\{z:w_z>0\}\) and \(W:=\sum_z w_z>0\). Assume global extendability in exactly the sense of accepted fact `b563a1eb51a20cd2`: there is a finite-valued function \(f:\mathbb R^n\to[0,\infty)\), agreeing with \(w\) at every integer point, including its zeros, such that \(f((1-t)x+ty)\ge f(x)^{1-t}f(y)^t\) for all real bases \(x,y\) and \(0<t<1\). A zero endpoint makes the right-hand side zero. No full-dimensionality assumption is made on \(A\), and all logarithms are natural.

For \(j\in A\), use \(\alpha_j(v):=\min\{w_{j+v},w_{j-v}\}\), \(\mathcal U_j:=\{v\in\mathbb Z^n:\alpha_j(v)>0\}\), and \(\Delta_j(v):=\log(w_j^2/(w_{j+v}w_{j-v}))\) for \(v\in\mathcal U_j\). Thus \(\alpha_j(v)\) is exactly the fixed-center \(\alpha(v)\) of accepted facts `280b299bc1e87c14`, `997f7c3a0c4804e4`, and `b563a1eb51a20cd2`, with its center displayed. For \(s\ge0\), retain their definitions

\[
B_j^\Delta(s):=\sum_{\substack{v\in\mathcal U_j\\\Delta_j(v)\le s}}\alpha_j(v),
\qquad K_j(w):=\max_{s\ge0}\frac{B_j^\Delta(s)}{1+s},
\qquad K(w):=\max_{j\in A}K_j(w).
\]

Every displacement sum here is oriented and includes zero unless explicitly excluded. The curvature is finite, nonnegative, and even on \(\mathcal U_j\), with \(\Delta_j(0)=0\). Each displayed maximum is attained. Define the new discounted quantities \(E_j:=\sum_{v\in\mathcal U_j}\alpha_j(v)e^{-\Delta_j(v)/2}\) and \(\mathscr R:=\sum_{j\in A}w_jE_j\). The exponent in \(E_j\) is \(-\Delta_j/2\), whereas the auxiliary \(\mathscr D_j\) in the proof of `997f7c3a0c4804e4` uses \(-\Delta_j\); these quantities are not identified.

For every nonzero \(v\in\mathbb Z^n\), call \(v\) primitive when \(\gcd(|v_1|,\ldots,|v_n|)=1\). For \(v\in\mathcal U_j\), put \(\tau_j(v):=\tfrac12\log(w_{j+v}/w_{j-v})\). Define

\[
\begin{aligned}
D_w&:=\sum_{j\in A}w_j^2,
&P_{\mathrm{tot}}&:=\sum_{j\in A}\sum_{v\in\mathcal U_j}w_{j+v}w_{j-v},\\
P_{\mathrm{prim}}&:=\sum_{j\in A}\sum_{\substack{v\in\mathcal U_j\\v\ \mathrm{primitive}}}w_{j+v}w_{j-v},
&P_{\mathrm{np}}&:=\sum_{j\in A}\sum_{\substack{v\in\mathcal U_j\setminus\{0\}\\v\ \mathrm{nonprimitive}}}w_{j+v}w_{j-v},\\
P_{\mathrm{bad}}(L)&:=\sum_{j\in A}\sum_{\substack{v\in\mathcal U_j,\ v\ \mathrm{primitive}\\|\tau_j(v)|>L}}w_{j+v}w_{j-v}
&& (L\ge0).
\end{aligned}
\]

In particular, \(P_{\mathrm{tot}}=D_w+P_{\mathrm{prim}}+P_{\mathrm{np}}\), and \(D_w\) is a diagonal product mass, not relative entropy. For \(b\in(\mathbb Z/2\mathbb Z)^n\), let \(W_b:=\sum_{z\equiv b\pmod2}w_z\) and \(q:=\sum_b(W_b/W)^2\), exactly as in `997f7c3a0c4804e4`. This scalar \(q\) is distinct from the thinning coefficients \(q_v\) in `280b299bc1e87c14`. The new \(P_{\mathrm{tot}}\) is exactly \(\sum_jw_jF_j\) for the \(F_j\) of `997f7c3a0c4804e4`.

To fix the normalization relative to `3bd24ddc8a30dd00`, specialize to its table \(w=\widetilde w\), with \(\widetilde w_z=e^{\lambda\cdot z}\) on \(P\cap\mathbb Z^n\) for its compact convex \(P\), and zero elsewhere. Then \(\Delta_j(v)=0\), \(\tau_j(v)=\lambda\cdot v\), \(W=\widetilde W\), \(E_j=\widetilde S_j\), \(\mathcal U_j\) is the predecessor's feasible displacement set, \(K(w)=\widetilde{\mathcal M}\), \(\mathscr R=\widetilde R\), \(D_w=\widetilde D\), and \((P_{\mathrm{tot}},P_{\mathrm{prim}},P_{\mathrm{bad}}(L))=(\widetilde T,\widetilde T_{\mathrm{prim}},\widetilde T_{\mathrm{bad}}(L))\). In general the product summand is \(w_{j+v}w_{j-v}=w_j^2e^{-\Delta_j(v)}\), so \(P_{\mathrm{tot}}\) must not be identified with the sum of midpoint squares \(\sum_{j\in A}\sum_{v\in\mathcal U_j}w_j^2\). Likewise, \(\mathscr R\) includes its stated curvature discount; it is not the raw weighted reflected-minimum mass in general.

For every such table,

\[
P_{\mathrm{tot}}=\sum_bW_b^2=qW^2\ge2^{-n}W^2,
\qquad E_j\le3K_j(w),
\qquad \mathscr R\le3K(w)W,
\qquad P_{\mathrm{np}}\le4(\mathscr R-D_w).
\tag{1}
\]

More precisely, put \(\gamma(L):=\max\{4,2+e^L\}\) for \(L\ge0\). Then

\[
\begin{aligned}
P_{\mathrm{tot}}-P_{\mathrm{bad}}(L)
&\le\gamma(L)\mathscr R-(\gamma(L)-1)D_w\\
&\le3\gamma(L)K(w)W-(\gamma(L)-1)D_w,
\end{aligned}
\tag{2}
\]

and consequently

\[
\begin{aligned}
K(w)
&\ge\frac{P_{\mathrm{tot}}-P_{\mathrm{bad}}(L)+(\gamma(L)-1)D_w}{3\gamma(L)W}\\
&=\frac{qW^2-P_{\mathrm{bad}}(L)+(\gamma(L)-1)D_w}{3\gamma(L)W}\\
&\ge\frac{2^{-n}W^2-P_{\mathrm{bad}}(L)+(\gamma(L)-1)D_w}{3\gamma(L)W}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{3}
\]

In particular, for fixed real constants \(L\ge0\) and \(\eta>0\), any class satisfying the retained-product condition \(P_{\mathrm{tot}}-P_{\mathrm{bad}}(L)\ge\eta\,2^{-n}W^2\) has \(K(w)\ge[\eta/(3\gamma(L))]2^{-n}W\). The more restrictive condition \(P_{\mathrm{bad}}(L)\le\rho\,2^{-n}W^2\), with a fixed \(\rho\in[0,1)\), is sufficient with \(\eta=1-\rho\). The exact retained-product condition preserves the parity surplus \(P_{\mathrm{tot}}-2^{-n}W^2\).

For the actual-body consequence, let \(n,d\ge1\), let \(C\subset\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^d\) be a convex body, and let \(S:=C\cap(\mathbb Z^n\times\mathbb R^d)\ne\varnothing\). Give \(C_z:=\{x\in\mathbb R^d:(z,x)\in C\}\), \(w_z:=\operatorname{vol}_d(C_z)\), \(W:=\sum_z w_z=\mathcal H_d(S)\), and \(h_S(p):=\inf_{H\ni p}\mathcal H_d(S\cap H)\) their exact canonical meanings from `280b299bc1e87c14`, with closed ambient halfspaces \(H\) and zero volume for empty or lower-dimensional fibers. If \(W>0\), its table satisfies all the hypotheses above. With \(\ell:=-\log(1-e^{-1})\), there is one point \(p^\star\in S\) such that, simultaneously for all real \(L\ge0\),

\[
h_S(p^\star)\ge\frac{\ell}{16}K(w)
\ge\frac{\ell\bigl(P_{\mathrm{tot}}-P_{\mathrm{bad}}(L)+(\gamma(L)-1)D_w\bigr)}{48\gamma(L)W}.
\tag{4}
\]

The point is selected before every halfspace, and can also be selected independently of the primitive tilt cutoff \(L\). Thus the retained-product condition with fixed \(L,\eta\) gives depth at least \([\ell\eta/(48\gamma(L))]2^{-n}W\) on the corresponding class of actual bodies. If that condition were established for every actual body with fixed absolute \(L,\eta\), it would prove the locked target with \(c_0:=\min\{\ell\eta/(48\gamma(L)),1/(2e)\}\). No such uniform resource condition is asserted here. If \(W=0\), the locked inequality holds at any point of the assumed nonempty \(S\), without defining any positive-center score.

The baseline bad-mass condition cannot hold on all globally extendable tables for any fixed \(L\ge0\) and \(\rho<1\): the exact ternary log-affine family in `3bd24ddc8a30dd00` has \(P_{\mathrm{bad}}(L)/(2^{-n}W^2)\to\infty\). This obstruction concerns the baseline bad-mass condition. It neither disproves a uniform lower bound for \(P_{\mathrm{tot}}-P_{\mathrm{bad}}(L)\) nor constitutes a counterexample to a scalar score bound or to the locked conjecture.
